company: Kelly (staffing agency; client = consumer/cooking appliance manufacturer)
role: Embedded Software Engineer (Embedded Systems Technician / Junior Embedded SW Engineer)
key_responsibilities: Support development, testing, and maintenance of embedded software applications
Program, modify, and debug software written in C
Analyze, troubleshoot, and resolve hardware and software issues in embedded systems
Read and interpret electronic schematics, wiring diagrams, circuit diagrams, block diagrams
Perform root cause analysis distinguishing hardware vs software faults
Support hardware teams through software investigation in a lab environment
Write technical specifications and documentation from product requirements
employment_type: W2 contract, 6 months to start, possible extension/conversion

strengths: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor - register-level C on Cortex-M4 (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1), timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven capture, custom low-level I2C driver, 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM, verified in Proteus. This is a near-exact match for the JD's core.

COFFIN capstone - 'Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture)'. Servo brown-out is a textbook hardware-vs-software isolation story, which is the JD's stated key focus.
Agnel Robotics Club - designed and fabricated single-layer PCBs in EAGLE, sensor comms over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback. Backs the schematic-reading and hands-on-hardware requirements.

BARC Python Developer Intern - PyQt/Matplotlib real-time data acquisition GUI in a laboratory environment, GitLab version control, technical documentation. Hits Python-preferred + docs-required + lab-environment in one entry.
B.E. Electronics & Telecommunication + M.S. Computer Engineering exceeds the preferred diploma/associate/bachelor's bar.
real_gaps: Zero consumer appliance / white goods domain exposure. Cooking ranges are safety-adjacent (gas valves, heating elements, certification constraints); the JD lists this as a plus but it shapes the day job.
Production lab troubleshooting at scale. Debugging experience is project-scale and self-owned, not sustaining-engineering on shipped hardware with formal RCA process and defect tracking.
Schematic reading is inferred from hobby-tier single-layer club PCBs, never claimed directly. Appliance control board schematics are a different density.
Test equipment listed as a tool line (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers) with no bullet demonstrating measurement-driven fault isolation.
overstated_by_keywords: FreeRTOS and STM32 on the Object Tracking Turret - per repo landmine notes the turret's embedded side is Arduino, not STM32/FreeRTOS. Do not lead with this under a depth probe.
Root cause analysis - counted as adjacent but never labeled as a process anywhere in the profile.
Technical specification writing - backed only by the Planctech claims documentation + BOM bullet.
llm_analysis.reasoning: On stated qualifications this is the cleanest match in the pipeline so far; every required bullet maps to real, defensible work, and the STM32 bare-metal project plus the COFFIN brown-out debugging story answer the JD's two hardest lines directly. The risk is not skill, it is structure: a 6-month W2 staffing contract in rural Tennessee against a pending EAD and a 90-day OPT unemployment cap, with a staffing-agency-to-appliance-manufacturer path that almost never produces H1B sponsorship. Overqualification is also a live screening risk - an M.S. CE profile heavy on CUDA and TensorRT reads as flight risk on a technician req unless the resume deliberately leads embedded.
